title: Iman Gadzhi's 17 laws of success: lessons from the top 1% he knows
summary: Iman shares 17 lessons from the wealthy people he knows. They cover buying assets with windfalls, doing the practical thing over the sexy one, discipline over motivation, small circles, radical responsibility, and compounding years of private work. Most of it is mindset and wealth habits rather than tactics.

principles.text: When a big sum of money lands, buy hard-to-sell assets so you can't spend it. In your first decades you are your own biggest liability.
principles.quote: you are a massive liability to yourself if you make a lot of money there's a high chance a high probability that you will spend it

principles.text: Make money in boring, practical businesses. Find inefficiencies and do something a few percent better, not a billion-dollar unicorn.
principles.quote: they just find areas in the market where there's inefficiencies or where they can just do something even three percent better and because of that they get more of the market shares

principles.text: Never be the first to name the price in a negotiation; talking less means fewer mistakes and more listening from others.
principles.quote: you should never ever be the first one to say the price when you're negotiating a deal

principles.text: Copy what successful people did at the start, not what they do now. Success is about doing things in the right order.
principles.quote: don't look at what a real estate agent is doing in their 15th year as being a real estate agent no look at what they did when they first started

principles.text: Rely on discipline, not motivation, because motivation is fleeting like a runner's high.
principles.quote: motivation is great sometimes you're gonna get it but it's fleeting you need to rely on discipline instead

principles.text: Winning is continuous: keeping and multiplying wins is harder than getting them, so don't rest on a win.
principles.quote: if you sleep on a win you're gonna wake up with a loss
